issue.title: W210 is silent on a read after a `foreach` over an empty list, although I230 already decides `[info exists x]` false there
issue.body:
## Repro

```tcl
proc p {} {
    foreach x {} {}
    if {[info exists x]} { puts yes }
    puts $x
}
foreach y {} {}
puts $y
```

Every tclsh from 8.4.20 to 9.1.0 raises `can't read "y": no such variable` (and the same for `x` when `p` is called): a `foreach` over an empty list never binds its variable.

`tcl diag` reports I230 "Condition '[info exists x]' is always false" — the existence fact holds `x` unbound after the zero-iteration loop — but no W210 on `puts $x`, nor on the top-level `puts $y`.

## Expected

W210 at both reads, from the same existence fact I230 decides the guard from. `docs/design/compiler/value-transfers-migration.md`'s W210 row states that W210 reads the existence fact.

## Where

`analyser/diagnostics/dataflow.rs`'s undef trace: the zero-iteration `foreach` is not a definition-free path for its loop variable in the trace, although the existence rung already holds the variable unbound there.

Pre-existing: the read was not reported at `6d214350b` either. Found by the final review of `claude/spectcl-optimization-discussion-5qhf42` (the bounded-loop worked example); not fixed there.
